sectors.name: Technology

sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in US semis (KLAC, SNDK) and Taiwan fab names (2303, 2454) on AI memory and HBM tightness; Indonesia tech remains laggard—overweight US/TW exposure via local custodians, trim ALAB/RUNS after 9%+ spikes into strength.

sectors.name: Financials
themes: Indonesian financials are decoupling from US counterparts, with local monetary stability and domestic credit demand providing a relative cushion against global rate shocks.
Insurance subsector is driving outsized gains (XCIS, LIFE, ASMI), reflecting structural under-penetration and rising middle-class demand for protection products.
Small-cap financials (ABDA, YULE, BEKS, LPGI) are seeing speculative retail inflows, creating volatility that institutional investors should exploit via selective entry, not blanket exposure.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to XCIS, LIFE, and ASMI on idiosyncratic catalysts, but keep overall financials underweight vs. index. The sector's flat aggregate masks a bifurcated tape: Indonesian names are outperforming US peers, yet the NORMAL signal argues against chasing broad beta. Rotate into high-momentum insurers and niche lenders, and trim laggards like BTPS if they fail to hold gains.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Coal exporters with integrated logistics and captive power are structurally advantaged as global supply constraints and Indonesian domestic market obligations keep margins sticky.
State-owned miners (PTBA) benefit from policy-driven volume targets and infrastructure spending, offering defensive cash flows amid commodity price volatility.
Nickel and downstream processing names (AADI) ride the EV battery supply chain reshoring wave, with Indonesia's ore export ban cementing local value-add as a durable growth driver.
sectors.ai: Buy selectively into coal names with captive power or export logistics (FPNI, DOID, BUMI) as ID outperformance persists despite weak US sentiment; momentum is broad but not euphoric, so rotate from laggards into leaders on pullbacks. Favor PTBA for state-backed volume upside and AADI for nickel-linked optionality, but trim any position if IDX energy reverses below its 20-day.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rural consumption recovery and government cash transfers are structurally lifting volume growth for mass-market FMCG players, favoring those with deep Java distribution networks.
Premiumization and health-conscious product shifts (functional foods, personal care) are creating durable margin expansion for brands that successfully innovate packaging and formulations.
E-commerce and quick-commerce penetration in tier-2/3 cities is reshaping FMCG go-to-market, giving agile local players a structural cost and speed advantage over legacy incumbents.
sectors.ai: Buy dips in FMCG small/mid caps with confirmed volume breakouts (MSJA, FOLK, KING) as domestic demand holds firm despite US softness; rotate out of laggards lacking earnings catalysts. Target names with strong rural distribution and digital channel growth, as sector consolidation and premiumization sustain momentum through 2H25.

themes: Indonesia's universal health coverage expansion and rising middle-class spending on private care are durable demand drivers for hospitals and pharma.
Government push for domestic vaccine and drug self-sufficiency (import substitution) structurally benefits local manufacturers like KAEF and MEDS.
Consolidation and digital health adoption across labs and diagnostics (LABS, IRRA) create scalable growth amid fragmented regional markets.

MEDS, SOHO, LABS, and KAEF show momentum from domestic demand and government health programs. Accumulate on dips; watch for profit-taking after sharp gains, but maintain overweight on structural growth.

sectors.name: Property & Real Estate
themes: Structural demand for industrial estates and data-center land in Greater Jakarta remains durable, driven by hyperscaler capex and logistics reshoring, benefiting DMAS and NIRO.
Landed residential developers with strong township pipelines (MSIE, KOTA) outperform as mortgage rates ease and middle-class housing backlog persists, unlike stratified high-rise segments.
Consolidation via M&A and land-bank revaluation is accelerating, favoring developers with prime locations and low leverage, while weak players face margin compression and inventory overhang.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to landed-residential and industrial developers (MSIE, NIRO, DMAS) on Jakarta land-bank scarcity and data-center demand; avoid high-rise laggards (BKDP, TARA) lacking presales momentum. Position into Q3 earnings for margin recovery, as rate-cut expectations and stable rupiah support refinancing. Trim MANG after its run; rotate to NIRO for recurring-income upside.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: AI-crypto convergence is now a durable narrative: compute, data, and inference tokens (TAO, ICP, NEAR) are pricing in real enterprise demand, not just speculation.
Interoperability and oracle layers (LINK, JUP) are structural winners as multi-chain activity and DeFi composability deepen, regardless of base-layer rotation.
Proof-of-work and high-throughput chains (KAS, MNT) benefit from a persistent institutional bid for 'digital commodity' exposure, decoupled from Ethereum-centric beta.
sectors.ai: Buy selective AI-infrastructure and interoperability tokens (ICP, TAO, NEAR, LINK) on strength; momentum is broad but not euphoric, so add on pullbacks rather than chase. Rotate out of laggards into leaders with real usage, and keep cash dry for a potential macro-driven dip. Indonesia's regulatory clarity is improving, but no local premium yet—position via global venues.
